title: Cycle Velocity Scenario Toolkit: Monte Carlo-based staffing & soft-decommit playbook
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Build a lightweight decision toolkit and playbook to surface plausible cycle velocity outcomes given staffing permutations, cross-team swaps, and soft-decommit triggers. The toolkit should let PMs and Eng leads run Monte Carlo scenarios, visualize probability of OKR completion, and produce a short actionable runbook: recommended hires/shadows, priority cuts with estimated customer impact, and a minimal communication template for stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: A web-accessible spreadsheet or small internal app that runs >=10k Monte Carlo trials with inputs: team FTE, fractionation (0-1), skill coverage, historical velocity distribution.
Output charts: completion probability vs time, burn-down fan, top-3 risk contributors, and recommended 1-3 scope trims with estimated delta to OKR likelihood.
Automation: ability to tag Linear issues (via API) as "soft-decommit candidate" based on a priority + size threshold and export a CSV for leads.
Runbook included (one-page) with step-by-step: when to escalate, how to apply soft-freeze, on-call shadow swaps, and communication templates for Exec/Customer-facing notices.
Two cross-functional reviews completed (Eng + Design + PM) and a trial run during mid-cycle review producing a recommended set of scope cuts for one initiative.
proposed_solution: Create a Google Sheet prototype (tabbed) with model parameters and charting, then wrap into a small internal node app for convenience. Use historical cycle velocities (last 8 cycles) as the prior distribution; allow manual override. Integrate a lightweight Linear action (script) that marks candidate issues and posts a summarized notification to #pm-cycle-runs on Slack.
tradeoffs: Sheet prototype is fast but limited (collaboration/scale). Full internal app requires infra and auth work (longer runway). Monte Carlo gives distributional insight but may lull teams into false precision — emphasize conservative policy bands. Tagging issues automatically accelerates ops but risks mass decommit suggestions; keep human-in-loop with approval step.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (sheet prototype, 2 weeks): collect velocity data from past cycles, build core Monte Carlo sampler, and create charts + decision outputs. Phase 2 (automation, 1 week): Linear tagging script and Slack summary. Phase 3 (internal app MVP, optional, 3-4 weeks): basic UI, stored scenarios, role-based access.
rollout_notes: Pilot with Platform PMs and two Eng leads during week 2 of cycle planning. Capture feedback, revise parameter defaults (skill friction, onboarding lag). Add a CI job that updates historical priors monthly.
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampler and bucket aggregation, QA run comparing sheet results to a small Python reference sampler. Run a retrospective A/B test: one initiative uses the toolkit then compare actual outcomes versus predicted bands.
monitoring_signals: Track usage (number of scenarios run), number of Linear issues tagged as candidates, % of suggested trims accepted, and post-cycle variance between predicted and observed velocity. Dashboards: sheet metrics + a simple Grafana panel on tagging webhook success.

risks: Overreliance on model outputs leading to aggressive cuts that harm long-term roadmap
Inaccurate priors due to inconsistent ticket sizing across teams
Automation labeling could create noise if approval flows aren't enforced
mitigation: Policy: always require Eng lead sign-off for any suggested decommit; script must open a review issue before tagging.
Normalize sizing: provide a small sizing conversion guide and run a quick cross-team calibration session ahead of runs.
Conservative defaults: show wide uncertainty bands and highlight "low-confidence" scenarios to decision-makers.
